name: When should I consider repairing my bathtub instead of replacing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider repairing my bathtub instead of replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Consider repairing your bathtub if the damage is localized and doesn't compromise the tub's structural integrity. Common repairable issues include surface chips, minor cracks, leaky faucets, or worn-out finishes. Replacement is generally recommended when the tub has extensive structural damage, severe and widespread cracks, persistent leaks that are difficult to isolate, or if you are planning a complete bathroom renovation and desire a different style or material. Repair is often more cost-effective for isolated problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair your bathtub for localized damage like chips, minor cracks, or leaks. Consider replacement for extensive structural damage, widespread cracks, or during a full renovation.
